# Alireza Ebrahimvandi, PhD

> Alireza Ebrahimvandi is a clinical AI data scientist at UCSF Health in San Francisco. He validates AI and machine-learning models for production use in a health system and monitors their performance after deployment, builds and evaluates large language model (LLM) summarization of inpatient clinical notes, and develops real-time bed-availability forecasting and patient-flow simulation for hospital operations. He holds a PhD in Industrial and Systems Engineering from Virginia Tech and has published peer-reviewed research applying machine learning and system dynamics to preterm birth, infant mortality, and PTSD.

Areas of expertise: clinical AI, healthcare AI model validation and post-deployment monitoring, LLM evaluation for clinical text, LLM-based clinical summarization and clinical-trial matching, predictive modeling for readmission and utilization risk, healthcare forecasting, discrete-event simulation, causal inference, and operations research.

## Publications

- [Identifying the Early Signs of Preterm Birth from U.S. Birth Records Using Machine Learning Techniques (Information, 2022)](https://doi.org/10.3390/info13070310): first author; code at https://github.com/ebrahimvandi/preterm_prediction
- [A DEA Evaluation of U.S. States' Healthcare Systems in Terms of Their Birth Outcomes (Expert Systems with Applications, 2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2021.115278)
- [Understanding State-Level Variations in the US Infant Mortality: 2000 to 2015 (American Journal of Perinatology, 2019)](https://doi.org/10.1055/s-0038-1675835): first author
- [Using a Stakeholder Analysis to Improve Systems Modelling of Health Issues (Systems Research and Behavioral Science, 2019)](https://doi.org/10.1002/sres.2563)
- [Group Model Building Techniques for Rapid Elicitation of Parameter Values, Effect Sizes, and Data Sources (System Dynamics Review, 2017)](https://doi.org/10.1002/sdr.1575)
- [A Dynamic Model of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder for Military Personnel and Veterans (PLOS ONE, 2016)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0161405)
- [Three Essays on Analysis of U.S. Infant Mortality Using Systems and Data Science Approaches (PhD dissertation, Virginia Tech)](https://hdl.handle.net/10919/96266)
